To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SU(3) LECs of order p 2, p 4, and p 6 can be expressed in terms of SU(2)-LECs plus a finite number of SU(3) counterterms.

(1) the SU(2)-LECs depend on m s in a simple and universal way, (2) this dependence can be expressed by means of the expansion of the SU(3)-LEC in powers of m s /Λ QCD, and that (3) the coefficients in the expansion can be calculated by means of the renormalization-group equations
(i) The SU(2)-LECs are functions of the strange quark and the light quark mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the low-energy constants which occur in the SU(2) chiral Lagrangian from the corresponding SU(3) quantities.
the question how the low-energy constants which are relevant at low energies in the chiral limit depend on the strange quarks mass.
the question of how to extract information on the low-energy constants from experimental data, and how to use this information for the analysis of the low-energy regime of QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dependence of the low-energy constants on the strange quarks mass is rather mild.
the SU(2) chiral expansion of QCD is a well defined expansion, and that the SU(3) chiral expansion, in the limit m s → ∞, is a consistent expansion, but it is a less well defined expansion.
chiral perturbation is a consistent framework, but that the SU(2)-LECs are not independent, and that they depend on the strange quarks masses, which in turn depend on the renormalisation scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at order p 4, the SU(2)-LECs are functions of m s only; and, at order p 6, the SU(3)- and SU(2)- LECs are related to each other in terms of m s.

the SU(2) low-energy constants are not universal, but depend on the heavy quark mass, and that the SU(3) low-energy constants can be obtained by a straightforward extrapolation of the SU(2)-couplings.
, in the chiral limit, the low-energy couplings of SU(2)-ChPT are independent of the strange quark.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SU(2) low-energy constants can be expressed in terms of SU(3)-low-energy constants, the strange-quark mass, and a few additional parameters.
the SU(3)-breaking effects are very small for the LECs which are relevant for the phenomenology of the low-energy constants.
, at order p 4, the dependence of the couplings on m s is rather weak, and that at order p 8 the dependence is even smaller.
